Based on the uploaded sources, here is the breakdown of how field seasonal performance (JAZ / SPF / WNG) depends on installation vintage, operational age, source type, and heat distribution system:

---

### 1. Dependence on Installation Year / Historical Vintage

* **Historical Fleet Evolution (1994/95 – 2002)**
  * **Source Title**: *FAWA – Feldanalyse von Wärmepumpen-Anlagen* (BFE / FWS, 2004)
  * **Section / Page**: Section 5.2.1 (p. 51, Abbildung 37) & Section 5.2.2 (p. 52–53, Abbildung 38)
  * **Building Type**: Single-family and multi-family residential buildings (< 20 kWth capacity)
  * **Data Year**: 1994/95 to 2002
  * **Sample Size**: **N = 221 installations** with climate-normalized data (out of 236 total)
  * **Values & Findings**:
    * Ground-source (Sole/Wasser) heat pumps showed an average efficiency improvement of **1.2% per installation year** (Abbildung 37).
    * Fleet-wide average JAZ across all newly installed Swiss heat pumps increased by **20%**, rising from **2.5** in 1994/95 to **3.0** in 2002 (Abbildung 38). This was driven by heat pump technical improvements (+15%) and an increasing market share of ground-source systems (rising from 28% in 1995 to 43% in 2002).

* **Modern Field Monitoring Campaign Evolution (2018 vs. 2021/22)**
  * **Source Title**: *Field Experience with Residential Heat Pumps in Switzerland...* (14th IEA Heat Pump Conference, Paper 478, 2023)
  * **Section / Page**: Section 3, Table 1 (p. 3 / p. 12)
  * **Building Type**: Single-family houses (new builds / renovations) and multi-family homes
  * **Data Year**: 2018
  * **Sample Size**: **N = 26 monitored systems** (14 air-to-water, 12 brine-to-water)
  * **Values**:
    * Air-to-water (AWHP) combined SPF (SH+DHW): **3.5** (new build), **3.1** (renovation), **2.8** (old build).
    * Brine-to-water (BWHP) combined SPF (SH+DHW): **4.9** (new build), **4.6** (renovation), **4.3** (old build).

  * **Source Title**: *Feldmessungen von Wärmepumpen-Anlagen Heizsaison 2021/22 (Jahresbericht)* (OST WPZ Buchs, 2022)
  * **Section / Page**: Zusammenfassung (p. 2) & Section 2.1 (p. 22, Abbildung 4 & 5)
  * **Building Type**: Single-family and multi-family residential buildings
  * **Data Year**: Heating season 2021/22
  * **Sample Size**: **N = 25 heat pump installations** (13 air-to-water, 12 ground-source) across 91 monitored heating seasons
  * **Values**:
    * Air-to-water (LW-WP) overall heat utilization factor (WNG) for combined heating + DHW averaged **3.10** (range: 2.36 at Obj 25 to 4.06 at Obj 15). Mean component JAZ+ = **3.34** (best: 4.24 at Obj 15).
    * Ground-source (SW-WP) overall WNG for combined heating + DHW averaged **4.23** (range: 3.00 at Obj 26 to 5.18 at Obj 21). Mean component JAZ+ = **4.48** (best: 5.46 / 5.63 at Obj 13).

---

### 2. Dependence on Operational Age (Aging / Degradation Over Time)

* **Source Title**: *FAWA – Feldanalyse von Wärmepumpen-Anlagen* (BFE / FWS, 2004)
* **Section / Page**: Section 10.1 (p. 91–92, Abbildung 113 & 114)
* **Building Type**: Single-family and multi-family residential buildings
* **Data Year**: 1995–2003 monitoring period
* **Sample Size**: Multi-year monitored sub-sample (9th operating year based on N = 1 for AWHP, N = 3 for SW-WP)
* **Values & Findings**:
  * **Air-Source (Luft/Wasser)**: Relative JAZ compared to Year 1 remains stable in Years 2–5 (**1.01–1.02×** of Year 1), with slight fluctuations in Years 6–9 (**0.96–0.98×** of Year 1) (Abbildung 113).
  * **Ground-Source (Sole/Wasser)**: Relative JAZ remains nearly constant across 9 operating years (**0.98–1.01×** of Year 1 performance), showing no significant long-term performance degradation (Abbildung 114).

---

### 3. Dependence on Source Type and Distribution System / Supply Temperature

* **Source Title**: *Field Experience with Residential Heat Pumps in Switzerland...* (14th IEA Heat Pump Conference, Paper 478, 2023)
* **Section / Page**: Section 3, Table 1 (p. 3 / p. 12)
* **Building Type**: Single-family houses (new builds / renovations) and multi-family homes
* **Data Year**: 2018
* **Sample Size**: **N = 26 monitored systems** (14 AWHP, 12 BWHP)
* **Space Heating Performance (SPF_SH)**:
  * **Underfloor Heating (35–30 °C design flow temp, New Buildings)**:
    * Air-to-Water (AWHP): **SPF_SH = 3.7**
    * Ground-Source / Brine-to-Water (BWHP): **SPF_SH = 5.7**
  * **Low-Temperature Radiators / Mixed (45–40 °C design flow temp, Renovations)**:
    * Air-to-Water (AWHP): **SPF_SH = 3.3**
    * Ground-Source / Brine-to-Water (BWHP): **SPF_SH = 5.0**
  * **Radiators (55–50 °C design flow temp, Old Buildings)**:
    * Air-to-Water (AWHP): **SPF_SH = 2.9**
    * Ground-Source / Brine-to-Water (BWHP): **SPF_SH = 4.4**

* **Supply Temperature Sensitivity Rule**:
  * **Source Title**: *FAWA – Feldanalyse von Wärmepumpen-Anlagen* (BFE / FWS, 2004)
  * **Section / Page**: Section 6.1 (p. 55)
  * **Building Type**: Single-family and multi-family residential buildings
  * **Data Year**: 1995–2003
  * **Sample Size**: **N = 221 installations**
  * **Values**: A **5 K increase** in mean supply flow temperature results in an average **8% reduction** in COP / JAZ. Renovated buildings with radiators had a 5 K higher supply temperature than new builds with underfloor heating, yielding a **9% lower JAZ**.

---

### 4. Domestic Hot Water (DHW) Mode Performance

* **Modern Monitored Fleet (2018 Data)**
  * **Source Title**: *Field Experience with Residential Heat Pumps in Switzerland...* (14th IEA Heat Pump Conference, Paper 478, 2023)
  * **Section / Page**: Section 3, Table 1 (p. 3 / p. 12)
  * **Building Type**: Single-family and multi-family residential buildings
  * **Data Year**: 2018
  * **Sample Size**: **N = 26 systems**
  * **Values**:
    * Air-to-Water (AWHP) in DHW mode: **SPF_DHW = 2.8**
    * Ground-Source (BWHP) in DHW mode: **SPF_DHW = 3.2**

* **Modern Monitored Fleet (2021/22 Heating Season)**
  * **Source Title**: *Feldmessungen von Wärmepumpen-Anlagen Heizsaison 2021/22 (Jahresbericht)* (OST WPZ Buchs, 2022)
  * **Section / Page**: Section 2.2 (p. 26, Abbildung 10 & 11)
  * **Building Type**: Single-family and multi-family residential buildings
  * **Data Year**: Heating season 2021/22
  * **Sample Size**: **N = 25 installations**
  * **Values**:
    * Air-to-Water (LW-WP) DHW mode: JAZ+_Aufladung ranged from **2.5 to 3.8** (mean **2.9**); WNG_Aufladung averaged **2.5** (15% lower due to standby & electric backup rod losses).
    * Ground-Source (SW-WP) DHW mode: JAZ+_Aufladung ranged from **1.6 to 4.8** (mean **3.3**); WNG_Aufladung averaged **2.9** (12% lower due to standby & electric backup rod losses). System utilization ratio SNG_TWW including tapping losses ranged from **0.64 to 2.84** (LW-WP) and **0.20 to 2.84** (SW-WP).

* **Historical FAWA DHW Configuration Breakdown**
  * **Source Title**: *FAWA – Feldanalyse von Wärmepumpen-Anlagen* (BFE / FWS, 2004)
  * **Section / Page**: Section 5.2 (p. 44, Table 3)
  * **Building Type**: Single-family house (Standard EFH 4-person)
  * **Data Year**: 1995–2003
  * **Sample Size**: **N = 236 installations**
  * **Values**:
    * Ground-source heat pump heating DHW via standard internal heat exchanger boiler: **JAZ_BWW = 3.4**.
    * Ground-source heat pump with solar thermal integration & combi-storage tank (*Kombispeicher*): **JAZ_BWW = 2.8**.
